title: CLO2024.2 - Attachment Simulation
description: CLO2024.2 brings more realistic simulation features! CLO technical experts will provide you with a detailed introduction to the new attachment simulation feature — attachments can perform realistic collision calculations with garments.
transcript:
In version 2024.2, Cloud's component simulation has been improved so that components are now affected by gravity and the interaction forces of the panels.  
These enhancements also make the display effect of the components more realistic. At the same time, the stability of component simulation has been greatly improved.  
We will demonstrate the functions after the improvement using the component on this suit.  
First, insert a component into the object window and attach it to the panel with a glue stick, then adjust its position.  
When you right-click the unit component, you will notice that the simulation option has been added to the right-click menu, and the component simulation state is divided into freeze, activate, and counter-activate.  
Since the glue tool is used at this time, you can see that the component simulation has been improved.  
The left-click unit component cannot switch to freeze or activate.  
When you use the right-click unit component to remove the glue, you can switch among the three simulation states.  
Select the activation option and start the simulation.  
After running the simulation, use grab to drag the component; you will see that it is presented under the effect of gravity and the interaction forces of the panel.  
The component will fall slightly due to gravity, and the interaction force between panels will suspend it by the panel.  
The effect on the real component and the panel is the same.  
The effect on the real component and the panel is the same.  
Additionally, the right-click component editor has been enhanced to include simulation of conflict thickness and rigidity.  
You can adjust the conflict thickness between the component and the panel by entering a value.  
In the previous version, components that did not use the glue tool after running the simulation were not affected by gravity.  
Therefore, they remained in their original position and did not fall under gravity.  
In component simulation, the connection is frozen, and it can be fixed to the component as in the previous version.  
Let's switch to another component.  
Right-click the component, choose freeze, and start the simulation.  
The component will not fall under gravity.  
Using grab to move the component, you can see that the interaction force between the component and the panel still exists.  
Unlike activation, after the component is frozen, you will see that the rigidity in the right attribute editor window is grayed out.  
This is because once the component is frozen, there will be no deformation.  
Therefore, the rigidity of the component cannot be changed.  
Depending on the component type, in version 2024.2, the component will be transformed by the interaction force between the component and the panel.  
First, the component must be in the activated state.  
Activate the component and check whether the simulated rigidity in the right attribute editor is applied.  
Rigidity refers to the stiffness level of the component.  
The default rigidity of the component is 50,000.  
The minimum value is 5,000.  
The maximum value can be set to 100,000.  
Then, when we reduce the rigidity of the component to 50,000,  
Then, when we reduce the rigidity of the component to 50,000,  
turn on the simulation.  
You will see that the component is more easily pulled and transformed by the force of the panel.  
On the other hand, if you want to set it as a solid component that is not easily deformed, you can increase its rigidity.  
You can adjust its rigidity according to the actual effect of the component.  
Finally, right-click the component, select reverse activation simulation.  
Turn on the simulation.  
The component remains in its original position.  
Use your hand to grab the component.  
You can see the interaction between the component and the panel.  
And the interaction effect in the 3D window has also disappeared.  
From this version onward,  
add-ons in the 3D window that are not attached to the board using the glue stick  
can also display the effect of the add-on under gravity.  
First, right-click the add-on and select Activate.  
Then select the add-on in the object window.  
Find the Weight option at the bottom of the attribute editor.  
At this point, the weight of the add-on is 7.6 grams.  
Simulate to check the effect of the add-on under the current weight.  
Then change the weight of the add-on to 50 grams,  
and simulate again.  
You will find that the add-on is more influenced by gravity.  
The above describes the new functions of our add-on simulation.  
It should be noted that the current add-on simulation is only suitable for CPU simulation.  
Based on this,  
you can set the hardness or weight of the add-on according to the type of add-on you want,  
and adjust it to make the display effect of the add-on simulation more realistic.

chunks.content: ## Component Simulation Enhancements in CLO 2024.2 This section covers the improved component simulation features in CLO version 2024.2, including gravity effects, panel interaction forces, simulation states, and enhanced stability, which collectively create more realistic component behavior. In CLO 2024.2, component simulation has been upgraded to incorporate gravity and interaction forces from panels, resulting in more realistic display effects. Stability of component simulation has also been significantly improved. ### Attaching Components and Simulation States To demonstrate the new features, insert a component into the object window and attach it to a panel using the glue stick tool. Adjust the component’s position as needed. Right-clicking the component reveals a new simulation menu with three states: - **Freeze**: Fixes the component in place, no gravity or deformation. - **Activate**: Enables gravity and interaction forces, allowing the component to move and deform. - **Counter-activate**: Reverses activation simulation effects, keeping the component stationary but responsive to interaction forces. Left-clicking the component does not allow switching simulation states; state changes must be done via right-click. When glued, components respond to gravity and panel forces during simulation. The component will slightly fall due to gravity but remain suspended by panel interaction forces, mirroring real-world behavior. ### Conflict Thickness and Rigidity Adjustments The right-click component editor now includes controls for **conflict thickness** and **rigidity**: - **Conflict Thickness**: Adjusts the space between the component and panel to avoid overlaps. - **Rigidity**: Defines the component’s stiffness and resistance to deformation during simulation. In previous versions, components not glued before simulation were unaffected by gravity and remained static. Now, components can be frozen to maintain a fixed connection, similar to past behavior. ## Simulation States and Their Effects This section details how each simulation state affects component behavior, including deformation, movement, and attribute availability. ### Freeze State Selecting **Freeze** and running the simulation prevents the component from falling due to gravity. The component remains fixed in place but still interacts with the panel via forces. In the attribute editor, **rigidity** is grayed out since the component cannot deform while frozen. ### Activate State and Rigidity Activating the component enables gravity and panel interaction forces to influence its movement and deformation. Rigidity controls how easily the component deforms: - Default rigidity: 50,000 - Minimum rigidity: 5,000 - Maximum rigidity: 100,000 Lower rigidity values make the component more flexible and prone to deformation by panel forces. Higher rigidity values make the component more solid and resistant to deformation. Adjust rigidity to achieve realistic component behavior based on the material or design intent. ### Counter-Activate State Selecting **Counter-activate** reverses the simulation activation. When simulation runs, the component remains in its original position, and interaction effects in the 3D window disappear. However, you can still grab and move the component to observe interaction forces. ## Add-On Simulation Features This section explains new add-on simulation capabilities in version 2024.2, including gravity effects and weight adjustments, enhancing realism for unattached 3D add-ons.

When simulation runs, the component remains in its original position, and interaction effects in the 3D window disappear. However, you can still grab and move the component to observe interaction forces. ## Add-On Simulation Features This section explains new add-on simulation capabilities in version 2024.2, including gravity effects and weight adjustments, enhancing realism for unattached 3D add-ons. From CLO 2024.2 onward, add-ons in the 3D window that are not attached to panels via the glue stick can also simulate gravity effects. ### Activating and Adjusting Add-Ons - Right-click the add-on and select **Activate**. - In the object window, select the add-on and locate the **Weight** attribute at the bottom of the attribute editor. - The default weight is 7.6 grams. - Run the simulation to observe the add-on’s behavior under this weight. - Increasing the weight (e.g., to 50 grams) results in stronger gravity effects on the add-on during simulation. ### Limitations and Recommendations Current add-on simulation is optimized only for CPU simulation. Users should set hardness and weight values according to the add-on type to achieve a realistic display effect in simulation. --- This documentation summarizes the key improvements and controls for component and add-on simulation in CLO 2024.2, focusing on gravity, interaction forces, simulation states, rigidity, and weight adjustments to facilitate realistic 3D garment assembly visualization.
